_comment: Model tier -> per-vendor model and effort. This is the cost-control dial. Re-audit every few months: the best-value model in each class drifts, and stale mappings quietly eat the savings. Change ids here, re-run build.py, no agent edits needed.
_principle: cheap fan-out, expensive judgment. Default agents to economy; spend reasoning only on ambiguous, cross-cutting, high-risk, or adversarial work where a wrong answer is expensive to detect.
_effort_note: Effort is the primary intelligence/latency/cost control on current Claude models, and effort names do not mean the same amount of thinking across models, so re-run the sweep per model against your own evals rather than carrying a setting over. Claude Fable 5.1 at low effort is often competitive on cost per task with a smaller model at higher effort while scoring higher, so include it in the comparison for the economy and standard tiers. Two effort side effects matter for this roster: at low effort a model reaches for search and read tools less (the scout and docs-writer prompts compensate by requiring a read before any claim), and at xhigh/max a model can draft a long deliverable in its thinking before writing it, so keep reasoning-tier agents at high unless an eval shows a gain.

economy._use: mechanical, high-volume, low-risk: scanning, extraction, mapping, boilerplate, doc synthesis. Failures are cheap to retry.

standard._use: clear-scope local reasoning where tests or review catch most mistakes: implementing a specified change, writing tests.

reasoning._use: ambiguous, cross-cutting, high-risk, long-horizon, or expensive-to-fix: architecture, adversarial review, security audit, planning and synthesis.
